properties.displayName: [IGNORE] GO-PRD-SENTINEL-142 Palo Alto Strata Logging Services - External Port Scanning Activity
properties.description:
The objective of this use case is to detect and monitor external port scanning activity against internal/private assets using Palo Alto Strata traffic logs ingested into Microsoft Sentinel.

This detection identifies suspicious external/public source IPs attempting to scan internal assets by either targeting multiple ports on a single internal destination (Vertical port scanning) or scanning multiple internal destinations on the same port (Horizontal port scanning) within a short time window.

The purpose of this use case is to identify potential external reconnaissance activity, early-stage attacker probing, unauthorized scanning attempts, and possible pre-exploitation behavior targeting internal network assets.
properties.query:
let VerticalThreshold = 150; 
let HorizontalThreshold = 10; // updated from 5 to 10
let ScanLookback = 5m;
let BinTimeBucket = 5m;
let AlertSuppressionTimeWindow = 24h;
let AllowedTrafficTimeWindow = 24h;
//
//Alert Suppression Block
let TriggeredIPs = SecurityAlert
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(AlertSuppressionTimeWindow)
    | extend RuleName = tostring(parse_json(ExtendedProperties).["Analytic Rule Name"])
    | where RuleName has "GO-PRD-SENTINEL-142 Palo Alto Strata Logging Services - External Port Scanning Activity" // Currenlty using has since rule name will be having ingore tag, before moving in prod chnge it to ==
    | extend SourceIP =tostring(parse_json(Entities)[0].Address)
    | where isnotempty(SourceIP)
    | distinct SourceIP;
//
//Vertical Port Scan - External source scanning multiple ports on same internal destination
let VerticalScan = GO_PaloAltoStrataLoggingService
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(ScanLookback)
    | where Activity == 'TRAFFIC'
    | where Action != "allow"
    | where isnotempty(DestinationPort) 
        and isnotempty(SourceIP) 
        and isnotempty(DestinationIP)
    | where not(ipv4_is_private(SourceIP)) and ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP)
    | summarize
        DistinctDestinationPortCount   = dcount(DestinationPort),
        PortSet         = make_set(DestinationPort, 50),
        Action          = make_set(Action),
        FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
        LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
        EventCount      = count()
        by SourceIP, DestinationIP, MF, bin(TimeGenerated, BinTimeBucket)
    | where DistinctDestinationPortCount >= VerticalThreshold
    | extend
        ScanType        = "External Vertical Port Scan",
        Description     = strcat("Single target ", DestinationIP, " scanned across ", DistinctDestinationPortCount, " ports"),
        IPCustomEntity  = SourceIP;
//
//Horizontal Port Scan - External source scanning many internal hosts on same port
let HorizontalScan = GO_PaloAltoStrataLoggingService
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(ScanLookback)
    | where Activity == 'TRAFFIC'
    | where Action != "allow"
    | where isnotempty(DestinationPort) 
        and isnotempty(SourceIP) 
        and isnotempty(DestinationIP)
    | where not(ipv4_is_private(SourceIP)) and ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP)
    | summarize
        DistinctDestinationIPCount       = dcount(DestinationIP),
        DestinationIPSet    = make_set(DestinationIP, 50),
        Action              = make_set(Action),
        FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
        LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
        EventCount = count()
        by SourceIP, DestinationPort, MF, bin(TimeGenerated, BinTimeBucket)
    | where DistinctDestinationIPCount >= HorizontalThreshold
    | extend
        ScanType        = "External Horizontal Port Scan",
        Description     = strcat("Single port ", DestinationPort, " scanned across ", DistinctDestinationIPCount, " hosts"),
        IPCustomEntity  = SourceIP;
//
// Union of both Scans
let ScannerResults = union VerticalScan, HorizontalScan
    | where SourceIP !in (TriggeredIPs);
//
// Combination of SourceIP and MF which will be correlated with allowed traffic
let ScannerPairs = ScannerResults
    | where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(MF)
    //| project SourceIP = tostring(SourceIP), MF = tostring(MF)
    | project SourceIP,MF
    | distinct SourceIP, MF;
//
//Allowed traffic check
let AllowedTrafficFromScanner = GO_PaloAltoStrataLoggingService
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(AllowedTrafficTimeWindow)
    | where Activity == 'TRAFFIC'
    | where Action == "allow"
    | where isnotempty(DestinationPort) 
        and isnotempty(SourceIP) 
        and isnotempty(DestinationIP)
        and isnotempty(MF)
    | where not(ipv4_is_private(SourceIP)) and ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP)
    //| extend SourceIP = tostring(SourceIP), MF = tostring(MF)
    | join kind=inner ScannerPairs on SourceIP, MF
    | summarize
        AllowedTrafficCount = count(),
        AllowedFirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
        AllowedLastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
        AllowedAction = make_set(Action)
        by SourceIP, MF;
//
// Final result
ScannerResults
| where not(ipv4_is_in_range(SourceIP, "64.39.102.0/24")) // Qualys Scanner IP range
| join kind = inner AllowedTrafficFromScanner on SourceIP, MF
| extend Action = set_union(Action, AllowedAction)
| project-away SourceIP1, AllowedAction, MF1

| where DisplayName == "GO-PRD-SENTINEL-035 Malware detected by PaloAlto Firewall" 
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(6h)
| extend A = parse_json(Entities) 
| mvexpand A
| extend IP = A.Address
| where isnotempty(IP)
| project IP;

| where TimeGenerated > ago (5m)
| where SourceIP !in (TriggeredIPs)

properties.displayName: UK-PRD-SENTINEL-115 Kerberoasting with WinEvent ID
properties.description: Kerberoasting with WinEvent ID
properties.query:
SecurityEvent 
| where EventID == 4769 
// Extract needed fields from XML when not parsed as columns 
| extend TicketEncryptionType = extract(@"<Data Name=""TicketEncryptionType"">([^<]+)</Data>", 1, EventData) 
| extend TicketOptions        = extract(@"<Data Name=""TicketOptions"">([^<]+)</Data>", 1, EventData) 
| extend ServiceName          = coalesce(ServiceName, extract(@"<Data Name=""ServiceName"">([^<]+)</Data>", 1, EventData)) 
| extend TargetUserName       = coalesce(TargetUserName, extract(@"<Data Name=""TargetUserName"">([^<]+)</Data>", 1, EventData)) 
| extend IpAddress            = coalesce(IpAddress, extract(@"<Data Name=""IpAddress"">([^<]+)</Data>", 1, EventData)) 
// Normalize common values 
| extend TicketEncryptionType = tostring(TicketEncryptionType) 
| extend TicketOptions        = tostring(TicketOptions) 
| extend IpAddress            = iff(IpAddress startswith "::ffff:", substring(IpAddress, 7), IpAddress) 
// Filtering logic 
| where isnotempty(TicketEncryptionType) and isnotempty(TicketOptions) 
| where TicketEncryptionType in ("0x17")    // RC4 
| where TicketOptions == "0x40810010"              // suspicious combo seen in tooling 
| where ServiceName !contains "$"                  // avoid machine accounts 
| summarize TotalRequests = count(), 
            DistinctIPs = dcount(IpAddress), 
            IPs = make_set(IpAddress, 10) 
          by TargetUserName, ServiceName, TicketEncryptionType, TicketOptions, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h) 
| where TotalRequests > 5

properties.displayName: UK-PRD-SENTINEL-008 EWT Mass secret retrieval from Azure Key Vault
properties.description:
Identifies mass secret retrieval from Azure Key Vault observed by a single user. 
Mass secret retrival crossing a certain threshold is an indication of credential dump operations or mis-configured applications. 
You can tweak the EventCountThreshold based on average count seen in your environment 
and also filter any known sources (IP/Account) and useragent combinations based on historical analysis to further reduce noise
properties.query:
let DistinctSecretsThreshold = 10;
let EventCountThreshold = 25;
// To avoid any False Positives, filtering using AppId is recommended.
// The AppId 509e4652-da8d-478d-a730-e9d4a1996ca4 has been added in the query as it corresponds to Azure Resource Graph performing VaultGet operations for indexing and syncing all tracked resources across Azure.
// The AppId 8cae6e77-e04e-42ce-b5cb-50d82bce26b1 has been added as it correspond to Microsoft Policy Insights Provider Data Plane performing VaultGet operations for policies checks.
let AllowedAppId = dynamic(["509e4652-da8d-478d-a730-e9d4a1996ca4","8cae6e77-e04e-42ce-b5cb-50d82bce26b1"]);
let AllowedObjectIds = dynamic(["82c6666a-74f8-4d83-a757-6bc96bb733a2", "884c2e8b-0c02-467e-905b-34b5f8cbfe74"]);
let OperationList = dynamic(["SecretGet", "KeyGet", "VaultGet"]);
AzureDiagnostics
| where OperationName in (OperationList) and ResourceType =~ "VAULTS"
| where not(identity_claim_appid_g in (AllowedAppId) and OperationName == 'VaultGet')
| extend
    ResourceId,
    ResultType = column_ifexists("ResultType", ""),
    identity_claim_http_schemas_microsoft_com_identity_claims_objectidentifier_g = column_ifexists("identity_claim_http_schemas_microsoft_com_identity_claims_objectidentifier_g", ""),
    identity_claim_http_schemas_xmlsoap_org_ws_2005_05_identity_claims_upn_s = column_ifexists("identity_claim_http_schemas_xmlsoap_org_ws_2005_05_identity_claims_upn_s", ""),
    identity_claim_oid_g = column_ifexists("identity_claim_oid_g", ""),
    identity_claim_upn_s = column_ifexists("identity_claim_upn_s", "")
| extend
    CallerObjectId = iff(isempty(identity_claim_oid_g), identity_claim_http_schemas_microsoft_com_identity_claims_objectidentifier_g, identity_claim_oid_g),
    CallerObjectUPN = iff(isempty(identity_claim_upn_s), identity_claim_http_schemas_xmlsoap_org_ws_2005_05_identity_claims_upn_s, identity_claim_upn_s)
| where not(CallerObjectId in (AllowedObjectIds) and OperationName == "SecretGet")
| as _Retrievals
| where CallerObjectId in (toscalar(
    _Retrievals
    | where ResultType == "Success"
    | summarize Count = dcount(requestUri_s) by OperationName, CallerObjectId
    | where Count > DistinctSecretsThreshold
    | summarize make_set(CallerObjectId,10000)
))
| extend
    requestUri_s = column_ifexists("requestUri_s", ""),
    id_s = column_ifexists("id_s", ""),
    CallerIPAddress = column_ifexists("CallerIPAddress", ""),
    clientInfo_s = column_ifexists("clientInfo_s", "")
| summarize
    EventCount = count(),
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTime = max(TimeGenerated),
    ResourceList = make_set(Resource, 50),
    OperationNameList = make_set(OperationName, 50),
    RequestURLList = make_set(requestUri_s, 50),
    ResourceId = max(ResourceId),
    CallerIPList = make_set(CallerIPAddress, 50),
    clientInfo_sList = make_set(clientInfo_s, 50),
    CallerIPMax = max(CallerIPAddress)
    by ResourceType, ResultType, identity_claim_appid_g, CallerObjectId, CallerObjectUPN
    | where EventCount > EventCountThreshold
| project-reorder StartTime, EndTime, EventCount, ResourceId,ResourceType,identity_claim_appid_g, CallerObjectId, CallerObjectUPN, ResultType, ResourceList, OperationNameList, RequestURLList, CallerIPList, clientInfo_sList
| extend timestamp = EndTime

properties.displayName: GO-PRD-SENTINEL-139 Potential Process Doppelganging
properties.description:
This rule detects potential process injection technique known as process doppelgänging, where adversaries may inject malicious code into process
order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. 
Process doppelgänging is a method of executing arbitrary code in the address space of a separate live process.   RITM1397976
properties.query:
let TriggeredUsers =
    SecurityAlert
    | where DisplayName == "GO-PRD-SENTINEL-139 Potential Process Doppelganging"
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(24h)
    | extend A = parse_json(Entities)
    | mvexpand A
    | extend User = A.Name
    | where isnotempty(User)
    | summarize make_list(User);
let RollbackEvents = SecurityEvent1 // Step 1: NTFS rollback events
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(10m)
    | where EventID == 4985 // NTFS transaction state changed (rollback)
    | where Account !in (TriggeredUsers)
    | where not (
                ((ProcessName has_any ("TiWorker.exe", "poqexec.exe", "trustedinstaller.exe")
        or ParentProcessName has_any ("TiWorker.exe", "poqexec.exe", "trustedinstaller.exe")))
        and CommandLine contains "WinSxS"
            )
    | project
        RollbackTime = TimeGenerated,
        Initiator = Account,
        InitiatorType = AccountType,
        TargetHost = Computer,
        RollbackProcessName = Process,
        RollbackProcessPath = ProcessName,
        EventID;
let ProcessCreation = SecurityEvent1 // Step 2: Suspicious process creation
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(10m)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has_any ("TxF", "Rollback", "Transaction")
    | where Account !in (TriggeredUsers)
    | where not (
                ((NewProcessName has_any ("TiWorker.exe", "poqexec.exe", "trustedinstaller.exe")
        or ParentProcessName has_any ("TiWorker.exe", "poqexec.exe", "trustedinstaller.exe")))
        and CommandLine contains "WinSxS"
            )

        ProcCreateTime = TimeGenerated,
        Initiator = Account,
        InitiatorType = AccountType,
        TargetHost = Computer,
        SuspiciousProcessName = NewProcessName,
        SuspiciousCommandLine = CommandLine,

    | where ObjectName has_any ("TxF", "Transaction")

| join kind=inner (ProcessCreation) on Initiator, TargetHost
| where abs(datetime_diff('minute', RollbackTime, ProcCreateTime)) <= 30
| join kind=inner (TxFCalls) on $left.Initiator == $right.Account and $left.TargetHost == $right.Computer

| extend TargetDevice = TargetHost, AccountName = Initiator, HostCustomEntity = TargetHost

    TargetDevice,
    AccountName,
    RollbackTime,
    ProcCreateTime,
    RollbackProcessName,
    RollbackProcessPath,
    SuspiciousProcessName,
    SuspiciousCommandLine,
    ParentProcessName,
    TxFCallCount
| order by ProcCreateTime desc

properties.description:
Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence is a platform that conducts threat infrastructure analysis and gathers threat intelligence.
This analytic identifies a match in SigninLogs on any IP Indicator of Compromise (IOC) from TI.
properties.query:
let queryFrequency = 1h;
let queryPeriod = 14d;
let qcMfaModChecks = qcMfaModificationChecks(); //call the workspace function
let mfaModTargetUserIds =
qcMfaModChecks
| distinct tostring(TargetId);
let AADFunction = (tableName:string){
    ThreatIntelligenceIndicator
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(queryPeriod)
    | where ExpirationDateTime > now()
    | summarize LatestIndicatorTime = arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IndicatorId
    | where Active == true
    // Pick up IOC alerts that contain entities of interest.
    | where isnotempty(NetworkIP)
        or isnotempty(EmailSourceIpAddress)
        or isnotempty(NetworkDestinationIP)
        or isnotempty(NetworkSourceIP)
    // Taking the first non-empty value (NetworkIP first) based on potential IOC match availability.
    | extend IpAddr = iff(isnotempty(NetworkIP), NetworkIP, NetworkDestinationIP)
    | extend IpAddr = iff(isempty(IpAddr) and isnotempty(NetworkSourceIP), NetworkSourceIP, IpAddr)
    | extend IpAddr = iff(isempty(IpAddr) and isnotempty(EmailSourceIpAddress), EmailSourceIpAddress, IpAddr)
    // Using innerunique join flavor to improve performance and only need one match.
    | join kind=innerunique (
        table(tableName)
        | where TimeGenerated >= ago(queryFrequency)
        | extend Status = parse_json(Status)
        | evaluate bag_unpack(Status)
        | extend ErrorCode = column_ifexists("errorCode", "")
        | extend AdditionalDetails = column_ifexists("additionalDetails", "")
        | extend FailureReason = column_ifexists("failureReason", "")
        | where UserId !in (mfaModTargetUserIds) //exclude accounts with recent mfa changes
        | where AdditionalDetails !in~ (
            "MFA not required during Windows broker logon flow" // MFA not required as IP already seen.
            "MFA completed in Azure AD" // User completed MFA in AAD.
        )
        // Remove AAD joined/registered devices.
        | extend Device = parse_json(DeviceDetail)
        | evaluate bag_unpack(Device, columnsConflict="replace_source")
        | extend TrustType = column_ifexists("trustType", "")
        | where TrustType !in~ (
        "Hybrid Azure AD joined",
        "Azure AD registered",
        "Azure AD joined"
        )
        // Filter out unsuccessful signins from TI feed.
        | where ErrorCode in (
            0,
            50125,
            50140,
            530002
        )
        | extend Location = parse_json(LocationDetails)
        | evaluate bag_unpack(Location)
        | extend State = column_ifexists("state", "")
        | extend City = column_ifexists("city", "")
        | extend Region = column_ifexists("countryOrRegion", "")
        | extend Location = strcat(City, ", ", State, " ", Region)
        | extend IpAddr = IPAddress
        // Renaming time column so log source clear.
        | extend SignInTimeGenerated = TimeGenerated
    ) on IpAddr
    | where SignInTimeGenerated < ExpirationDateTime
    | summarize SignInTimeGenerated = arg_max(SignInTimeGenerated, *) by IndicatorId, IpAddr
    | where ConfidenceScore >= 90
| project
    SignInTimeGenerated,
    Description,
    ActivityGroupNames,
    IndicatorId,
    ThreatType,
    Url,
    ExpirationDateTime,
    ConfidenceScore,
    IpAddr,
    UserName = Identity,
    UserPrincipalName,
    UserId,
    UserAgent = UserAgent1,
    AppDisplayName,
    AppId,
    Location,
    ErrorCode,
    AdditionalDetails,
    FailureReason,
    NetworkIP,
    NetworkDestinationIP,
    NetworkSourceIP,
    EmailSourceIpAddress,
    Type
};

properties.description:

properties.query:
let dt_lookBack = 1h;

// Union safeline to prevent errors if watchlist unavailable.
let safeline = datatable(SearchKey:string)[];
let watchlist = union isfuzzy=true safeline, _GetWatchlist("ThreatIntelEntityExclusions");
//Create a list of TLDs in our threat feed for later validation of extracted domains
let list_tlds = ThreatIntelligenceIndicator
| where TimeGenerated > ago(ioc_lookBack)
| where isnotempty(DomainName)
| extend DomainName = tolower(DomainName)
| extend parts = split(DomainName, '.')
| extend tld = parts[(array_length(parts)-1)]
| summarize count() by tostring(tld)
| summarize make_list(tld);
ThreatIntelligenceIndicator
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(ioc_lookBack) and ExpirationDateTime > now()
| summarize LatestIndicatorTime = arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IndicatorId
| where Active == true
// Picking up only IOC's that contain the entities we want
| where isnotempty(DomainName)
| where DomainName !in (watchlist)
// using innerunique to keep perf fast and result set low, we only need one match to indicate potential malicious activity that needs to be investigated
| join kind=innerunique (
    xw_CommonSecuritylog
    | extend IngestionTime = ingestion_time()
    | where IngestionTime > ago(dt_lookBack)
    //Extract domain from RequestURL, if not present extarct it from AdditionalExtentions
    | extend PA_Url = columnifexists("RequestURL", "None")
    | extend PA_Url = iif(isempty(PA_Url) and AdditionalExtensions !startswith "PanOS", extract("([^\"]+)", 1, tolower(AdditionalExtensions)), trim('"', PA_Url))
    | extend PA_Url = iif(PA_Url !startswith "http://" and ApplicationProtocol !~ "ssl", strcat('http://', PA_Url), iif(PA_Url !startswith "https://" and ApplicationProtocol =~ "ssl", strcat('https://', PA_Url), PA_Url))
    | extend Domain = trim(@"""",tostring(parse_url(PA_Url).Host))

    //Split out the TLD for the purpose of checking if we have any TI indicators with this TLD to match on
    | extend tld = parts[(array_length(parts)-1)]
    //Validate parsed domain by checking TLD against TLDs from threat feed and drop domains where there is no chance of a match
    | where tld in~ (list_tlds)
    | extend CommonSecurityLog_TimeGenerated = TimeGenerated
    ) on $left.DomainName==$right.Domain
| where CommonSecurityLog_TimeGenerated < ExpirationDateTime
| summarize CommonSecurityLog_TimeGenerated = arg_max(CommonSecurityLog_TimeGenerated, *) by IndicatorId, FileHashValue
| project CommonSecurityLog_TimeGenerated, Description, ActivityGroupNames, PA_Url, Domain, IndicatorId, ThreatType, ExpirationDateTime, ConfidenceScore, DeviceAction, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DeviceName, SourceIP, SourcePort, ApplicationProtocol, RequestMethod

properties.displayName: QC - D - gsecdump artifact dropped on disk
properties.description:
The query identifies suspicious binaries that perform the WriteToLsassProcessMemory action type on the target system.
This behaviour has been seen when credential dumping tools are used. A "High" Integrity Level is required to dump
credentials successfully. Advanced adversaries may change the name of the binary or modify the source code to perform
credential dumping attacks.
References:
- https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/
- https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0008/
- https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=HackTool:Win32/Gsecdump

let GsecDumpIoCSearch = 
(union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(TimeFrame)
| where ActionType has_any ("OpenProcessApiCall", "CreateRemoteThreadApiCall", "ReadProcessMemoryApiCall", "NtAllocateVirtualMemoryRemoteApiCall")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex "(^[0-9-a-z]{8})-([0-9a-z]{4})-([0-9a-z]{4})-([0-9a-z]{4})-([0-9a-z]{12}).exe"
| join (
  DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(TimeFrame)
  | where ActionType has "WriteToLsassProcessMemory"
  | where (AccountDomain == "" and isempty(AccountName) 
      and isempty(FileName) and isempty(FolderPath) 
      and isempty(ProcessCommandLine) and isempty(ProcessId) 
      and isempty(ProcessTokenElevation))) on DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessParentId

              InitiatingProcessParentId = make_set(InitiatingProcessParentId), InitiatingProcessId = make_set(InitiatingProcessId),

properties.displayName: QC - D - Suspicious Terminal Services service started
properties.description:
This query identifies any new service started utilizing the net command. Additionally, it looks for the particular
case of Terminal Services (TermService) service enabling.
Adversaries may abuse the Windows service control manager to execute malicious commands
or payloads. The Windows service control manager (services.exe) is an interface to manage and manipulate services.
The service control manager is accessible to users via GUI components as well as system utilities such as sc.exe
and Net. Adversaries may try to get information about registered services. Commands that may obtain information
about services using operating system utilities are "sc," "tasklist /svc" using Tasklist, and "net start" using Net,
but adversaries may also use other tools as well. Adversaries may use the information from System Service Discovery
during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target
and/or attempts specific actions.
Reference:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1007/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0039/
  - https://www.windows-commandline.com/start-terminal-services-command-line/
properties.query:
let net_params = dynamic (["start TermService"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where ActionType has "ProcessCreated"
| where FileName has_any ("net", "net1") 
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (net_params)
| summarize FileName = make_set(FileName), ProcessId = make_set(ProcessId), InitiatingProcessParentId = make_set(InitiatingProcessParentId), InitiatingProcessId = make_set(InitiatingProcessId), 
          count() by DeviceName, ActionType, 
                      InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName,  
                      InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel, ProcessTokenElevation, 
                      AccountDomain, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountDomain, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel, InitiatingProcessTokenElevation
| project-reorder DeviceName, ActionType, 
                InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName,  FileName, 
                ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessParentId, InitiatingProcessId,
                ProcessIntegrityLevel, ProcessTokenElevation, 
                AccountDomain, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountDomain, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel, InitiatingProcessTokenElevation

properties.displayName: QC - D - Scheduled malicious file
properties.description:
This query will look for Redline task scheduler creations to run malicious files under temp folder every 5 minutes 
'“C:\Windows\System32\schtasks.exe" /Create /SC MINUTE /MO 1 /TN mnolyk.exe /TR "C:\Users\admin\AppData\Local\Temp\4b9a106e76\mnolyk.exe" /F."'
It will help Threat hunters find file creation events associated mentioned file path.
References:
- https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/
- https://www.socinvestigation.com/redline-stealer-returns-with-new-ttps-detection-response/
properties.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h) 
| where FileName == "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "sc" and ProcessCommandLine has "create"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !contains "system"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"C:\\Users\\[a-zA-Z0-9_]+\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\[a-zA-Z0-9_]+\\[a-zA-Z]+\.exe$"

properties.displayName: QC - D - QR code recieved via email
properties.description:
This query looks for quishing emails recieved that contains a picure QR code with random alpha characters as a filename and an image type of PNG.
Hunters should review any results and soft or hard delete recieved emails of concern.
Ref: https://www.trustwave.com/en-us/resources/blogs/spiderlabs-blog/think-before-you-scan-the-rise-of-qr-codes-in-phishing/
properties.query:
let TimeFrame = 1h;
EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(TimeFrame)
| where FileType contains "png"
| where FileName matches regex @'^[A-Z0-9]{9,10}\\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$'
| where RecipientObjectId != ""
| join EmailEvents on NetworkMessageId
| where DeliveryAction != "Blocked"
| where DeliveryAction != "Junked"

properties.displayName: QC - D - PowerShell or Python execution via AppleScript
properties.description:
Adversaries use Python based C2 frameworks such as Empire that can execute PowerShell commands etc. on a MacOS device depending on the installation. This detection aims to detect usage of Empire payloads that utilize AppleScript binary that runs Python commands/PowerShell commands. Base64 encoded commands can also be executed via AppleScript on MacOS devices. This query aims to detect the same. 
References:
- https://medium.com /purple-team/creating-malicious-payloads-for-mac-osx-using-empire-tool-f9024432e2dc
- https://github.com/EmpireProject/Empire
properties.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp >= ago(1h)
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("installer", "Snap Camera"))
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName contains "PanGpHip" or InitiatingProcessParentFileName contains "PanGpHip" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "GlobalProtect")
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "osascript -e" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("shell script", "echo", "import sys", "base64")) 
or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "osascript -e" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_all ("shell script", "echo", "import sys", "base64"))

properties.displayName: QC - D - Detect suspicious process created accessing LSA Secrets
properties.description:
Adversaries with high privilege access to a host may attempt to access Local Security Authority (LSA) secrets, 
which can contain a variety of different credential materials, such as credentials for service accounts.
LSA secrets are stored in the registry at HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SECURITY\Policy\Secrets. 
Advanced adversaries may use the secrets key to assist with extracting passwords and enumerating other sensitive
system information.
Please take in mind that LSA secrets can also be dumped from memory.
References:
- https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/004/
- https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0002/
- https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0029/
properties.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where ActionType has "ProcessCreated"
| where InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel in ("High", "system") 
| where ProcessCommandLine has @"HKLM\security\policy\secrets"
| summarize InitiatingProcessFolderPath = make_set(InitiatingProcessFolderPath), FileName = make_set(FileName), FolderPath = make_set(FolderPath), 
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),ProcessCommandLine = make_set(ProcessCommandLine), 
          InitiatingProcessParentId = make_set(InitiatingProcessParentId), InitiatingProcessId = make_set(InitiatingProcessId), ProcessId = make_set(ProcessId), 
          count() by DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, 
                      AccountDomain, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountDomain, InitiatingProcessAccountName, 
                      InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel, ProcessIntegrityLevel
| project-reorder DeviceName, ActionType, count_, 
                  InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,  InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, 
                  InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine, 
                  InitiatingProcessParentId, InitiatingProcessId, ProcessId,
                  AccountDomain, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountDomain, InitiatingProcessAccountName, 
                  InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel, ProcessIntegrityLevel
